note: The frog's life stages (schema/SPECIES_STAGES.md), kept by hand. tools/build_xenopus_atlas.py reads this block, checks each number against the saved running text of the open paper it cites, and writes it into data/species/xenopus.json with those papers among the species' sources: edit it here, then build. Two stages are drawn, the fertilised egg and the adult (the file's own); four are named and not drawn. The species opens on its adult. One stage gives a word of its own for what Cells models of it: the fertilised egg, planned, with its record (decided on 19 November 2026, the engine's lead agreeing that the record supports the word); every other stage takes the species' own word.

list.label: Fertilised egg
list.plain: The fertilised egg: one cell, before its first division.
list.no_further_levels: A fertilised egg is one cell: it has no tissue, organ or body yet.

modelled.text: The project's record decides that the frog's early cleavage, from one cell to four, is the first subject of its cell-division work (D141, D144, the cell-division plan). That work's design note is on main, and so far the engine has carried an egg-scale cell through prescribed division against independently written references (the Engine view's Cell division S2–S5a). The record's first prediction for the egg itself, J1, its membrane potential at the onset of second cleavage, was made with an independent reference model and misses the measured value (12 November 2026); no engine run of it exists. No model of this egg is registered, so the word here is the lower one the record allows: planned. What is drawn is a generic cell's parts at the egg's size.

record.where: D144: Qualify the simulator for many uses, not one experiment
Order of work (lead's ranking under D141), item 2: Xenopus early cleavage first, from 1 to 4 cells
Its status line: draft for review; nothing here is built or qualified
Cell division S0b: J1 prediction of record and verdict; J1 fails on the reference (12 November; development)

levels.label: The egg
levels.note: The egg is drawn as a sphere 1.2 mm across, the diameter a review gives the frog's fertilised eggs. What is drawn inside it is not the egg's own structure: its parts are the generic cell's, the parts of the frog's skin-like cell drawn here, enlarged to the egg's size. An egg's yolk, its pigment and the rest of what it holds are not drawn.

notes.text: Its parts are a generic cell's, enlarged: not the egg's own; its yolk and pigment are not drawn
notes.short: A generic cell's parts, enlarged: not the egg's own

facts.label: Diameter
facts.value: about 1.2 mm, as a review gives the frog's fertilised eggs

cap.junctions.why: The egg is one cell: it has no neighbour to share a junction with.

list.label: Two-cell embryo

time.where: the section "NF stages 1-6: zygote and cleavage", paragraph 1, which gives the time of the first cell division

list.note: The time is that of the first cell division, after which the embryo is in two cells.
list.missing: No size of the two-cell embryo is in hand under usable terms, and nothing of it is drawn.

list.label: Four-cell embryo
list.note: The paper gives this stage's time from the first division, not from fertilisation (20 to 30 minutes after it, at 23 °C), so no time is written for it here.
list.missing: No size of the four-cell embryo is in hand under usable terms, and nothing of it is drawn.

list.label: Free-swimming tadpole
list.plain: The stage at which tadpoles break free of the vitelline membrane and begin to swim.
list.missing: No length of a tadpole at this stage is in hand under usable terms, and nothing of it is drawn.

list.label: End of metamorphosis
list.plain: The froglet, its tail fully resorbed.
list.missing: No size of the froglet is in hand under usable terms, and nothing of it is drawn.
